a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: The query is a fully ionized zwitterion at physiological pH (neutral fraction 0, estimated logD -3.31, TPSA 150.22) carrying a benzamidine and a propionic acid; this is the same ionizable pharmacophore as melagatran, whose measured Caco-2 Papp was 0.03 ± 0.01 ×10^-6 cm/s (C129), indicating a severe passive-permeability barrier.

Other amidine-containing reference molecules also show very low apical-to-basolateral permeability: bisamidine prodrug 2 had Papp 1.86 ± 1.19 ×10^-8 cm/s (C108, C148), increasing only to 4.42 ± 0.43 ×10^-8 cm/s with P-gp inhibition (C104, C116), and BRACO19 showed no detectable A→B transport at 4°C (C145).

L4 solubility records for FX-93 (C118, C126, C134, C120, C109) and M05/M11 (C127, C103) show good aqueous solubility for some related ionizable molecules, but solubility alone does not overcome the measured permeability barrier and does not provide F >= 20% evidence.
No L4 record reports a direct oral bioavailability value for the query or a close analog; permeability and solubility are absorption components, not systemic F measurements.
